subject: af-td
title: AF.TD.------AFI(1)
description: Diagram in AF(D)-21 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's diagnostic that 'the solidification of alternative viewpoints cannot affect the basic lining of western culture — and because of this, positive transformation is negated (or stopped)' under suppressed affinity dynamics. (C)AF-TD (the concept of affinity-tendency) is crossed with AFI(1) (affinity insight, first-order): the question is what affinity-tendency produces when crossed with first-order affinity-insight — the (1) marker on AFI being load-bearing, distinguishing primary affinity-insight from secondary (AFI2) which appears elsewhere in the glossary. VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) sits between subject and partner. PER-TRS (perceived transference) anchors the upper-right output. SOC-RT-P (social reality particulars) hangs on the right margin. (R)TM (the reality of time) feeds in from the lower-left. SF-RZ (surface realization) sits below the subject. IST-F (interior-source functionalism) and AFL (affinity alignment) form the lower-center. ACT-T (actual terms) anchors the lower-right via a *dashed* edge to ALT-F (alternative functionalism). Structural argument: affinity-tendency crossed with first-order-affinity-insight produces perceived-transference as upper output and social-reality-particulars as right output. The dashed edge between ACT-T and ALT-F is load-bearing: it exposes Braxton's structural verdict that *actual* alternative-functionalism is only conditionally achievable from actual-terms — the suppression Braxton names operates precisely by breaking that dashed link, making alternative-functionalism appear unreachable from any actual ground.
